{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>MUTUAL SECRECY AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>This AGREEMENT effective as of the 17th day of May, 1996, is between UCAR CARBON COMPANY INC., a Delaware corporation, having offices at 39 Old Ridgebury Road, Danbury, Connecticut O68l7 (hereinafter referred to as "UCAR CARBON"); and BALLARD POWER SYSTEMS INC., having an office at 9000 Glenlyon Parkway, Burnaby, B.C. Canada V5J 5J9 (hereinafter referred to as "BALLARD").</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>WHEREAS, UCAR CARBON possesses certain proprietary information (hereinafter UCAR CARBON Proprietary Information) relating to the manufacture of flexible graphite for use in fuel cells:</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>WHEREAS, BALLARD possesses certain proprietary information (hereinafter BALLARD Proprietary Information) relating to fuel cells and components for fuel cells.</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>WHEREAS, UCAR CARBON and BALLARD desire to exchange such proprietary information (hereinafter individually and collectively referred to as "Proprietary Information") for the purpose of UCAR CARBON supplying flexible graphite produced employing UCAR CARBON Proprietary Information to BALLARD under a separate purchase order.</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>WHEREAS, each party is willing to disclose to the other party its Proprietary Information for the specific purposes of this Agreement under the following conditions:</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>1. During the term of this Agreement, the receiving party agrees to hold in confidence and not disclose to any person or persons, other than its employees with a need to know, or use except for the purpose of this agreement, for a period of fifteen (15) years from the date of each disclosure, any and all Proprietary Information disclosed in writing and identified as Proprietary Information by the disclosing party. </SPAN 6><SPAN 7>If Proprietary Information is disclosed orally or in other than written form, it must be identified as Proprietary Information at the time of disclosure and summarized in writing and identified as Proprietary Information by the disclosing party within thirty (30) days from the date of the disclosure. </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>It is understood that the foregoing obligation of confidentiality does not apply to:</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>a) information which at the time of disclosure is in the public domain;</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>b) information which is published or otherwise becomes part of the public domain through no fault of the receiving party after the disclosure hereunder;</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>c) information which the receiving party can demonstrate by reasonably convincing evidence is already known or in the possession of the receiving party at the time of disclosure hereunder;</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>d) information that the receiving party can show was received by it after the time of the disclosure hereunder from a third party on a non-confidential basis who did not acquire such information directly or indirectly from the disclosing party under an obligation of confidence; or</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>e) information that is developed by an employee of the receiving party independent of any such disclosure under this Agreement.</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>2. The receiving party agrees to use at least the same degree of care in maintaining the other party's Proprietary Information confidential as it does for maintaining the confidentiality of its own Proprietary Information of a similar nature.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>3. The receiving party agrees not to copy any Proprietary Information without the written permission of the disclosing party, and shall return such Proprietary Information and any copies when requested to do so by the disclosing party during the term of this Agreement</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>4. No license, express or implied, is granted by either party to the other party under any patent, trade secret or copyright now or hereafter owned by either party under this Agreement.</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>5. This Agreement shall be construed and interpreted, and its performance shall be governed by substantive laws of the state of Connecticut, U.S.A., without recourse to its conflict of laws, rules or principles. </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>6. Either party upon thirty (30) days notice given in writing to the other party may terminate this Agreement. </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>However, termination of the Agreement will not affect the confidentiality and non-use obligations of either party.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>AGREED:</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>BALLARD POWER SYSTEMS INC. </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>UCAR CARBON COMPANY INC.</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>By /s/ Keith B. Prater By/s/ R.M. Flowers</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>Name Keith B. Prater Name R.M. Flowers</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>Title Vice President Title Dir.-Worldwide Tech.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>Date 21Jun96 </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>Date July 2, 1996</SPAN 27>

Let's start with the first hypothesis, nda-11: "Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information." The NDA doesn't mention reverse engineering anywhere. The relevant sections talk about confidentiality, use, and disclosure but not reverse engineering. So this is NotMentioned.

Next, nda-16: "Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement." The document mentions termination in section 18 and 19. Section 19 says termination doesn't affect confidentiality obligations, but section 15 talks about returning Proprietary Information upon request. However, the termination trigger isn't explicitly linked to destruction or return. The skill for termination-triggered-return might apply here, but the evidence isn't clear. So maybe NotMentioned or Contradiction? Wait, the skill mentions that the source should explicitly state the return or destruction upon termination. The document doesn't have that exact language, so it's NotMentioned.

nda-15: "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information." Section 16 clearly states no license is granted. That's a direct match. So Entailment with evidence from span 16.

nda-10: "Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated." The NDA doesn't mention confidentiality of the agreement's existence. The skill for negotiation-existence-secrecy requires explicit prohibition. Since there's no such clause, NotMentioned.

nda-2: "Confidential Information shall only include technical information." The NDA refers to Proprietary Information but doesn't specify it's only technical. No mention of non-technical info, so NotMentioned.

nda-1: "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." Sections 6 and 7 mention identification, both written and oral. So Entailment with spans 6 and 7.

nda-19: "Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement." Section 19 states confidentiality obligations survive. Entailment with span 19.

nda-12: "Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information." Section 13 says developed info by the receiving party is excluded. So Entailment with span 13.

nda-20: "Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information." Section 15 says they must return upon request, but there's no mention of retaining. The skill for express-retention-carveout might apply, but the evidence isn't there. So NotMentioned.

nda-3: "Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information." Section 7 mentions oral disclosure needing identification. So Entailment with span 7.

nda-18: "Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives." No mention of solicitation, so NotMentioned.

nda-7: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties." Section 6 allows sharing with employees with a need to know, but not third-parties. So Contradiction? Wait, the hypothesis is about third-parties. The NDA doesn't mention third-parties, so NotMentioned.

nda-17: "Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances." Section 15 says they can't copy without permission. But the skill for copy-clause-polarity-inspection might apply. The clause says they agree not to copy without permission, which implies that copying is allowed with permission. So Entailment with span 15.

nda-8: "Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law to disclose any Confidential Information." No mention of legal requirements, so NotMentioned.

nda-13: "Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party." Section 12 allows info from third parties if not confidential. So Entailment with span 12.

nda-5: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees." Section 6 allows sharing with employees with a need to know. Entailment with span 6.

nda-4: "Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement." Section 6 says use is limited to the purpose of the agreement. Entailment with span 6.

guidance.inspection: Separate the operative return or destruction duty from request-only duties, then verify that the stated trigger is an ending event and carry forward any scope limits or exceptions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the ending-event trigger together with the operative return or destruction language; include a governing list introduction when the duty is an item.

guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention permission and any governing exception transition, plus material limits such as archival-only access, dispute purpose, or continuing confidentiality.

guidance.when: The source expressly prohibits disclosure of the existence or occurrence of negotiations, discussions, an agreement in progress, receipt of evaluation material, or terms or status of the contemplated transaction.
guidance.inspection: Distinguish secrecy of the deal process or agreement facts from ordinary secrecy of confidential information, and preserve consent, audience, and publicity qualifications.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition's governing language and each relied-on enumerated subject; a generic nondisclosure clause alone is insufficient.

guidance.when: A source clause expressly addresses making, reproducing, automatically creating, returning, destroying, or retaining copies of protected information.
guidance.inspection: Classify the copy language by legal function: affirmative exception, automatic-copy acknowledgement, consent-conditioned prohibition, mere reference to existing copies, return duty, or retention carve-out. Do not infer creation permission from employee access or generic safeguarding.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative copy wording and its governing condition or exception; read adjacent retention or return language when it changes the clause's function.

guidance.when: The source expressly states that the agreement or disclosure grants, conveys, or confers no right or license in protected information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Identify the denied grant separately from ownership, limited-purpose use, and review permissions; preserve any express narrow exception without treating it as a general license.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative no-rights or no-license wording and any material exception; ownership language may be retained as independent support but is not a substitute for an express grant denial.

guidance.when: The source expressly limits use of protected information to a stated agreement, transaction, evaluation, project, discussion, or business-relationship purpose, whether phrased as 'only' or as a prohibition with a necessary-purpose exception.
guidance.inspection: Treat the permitted purpose as the boundary of the restriction, not as permission for unrelated uses; capture both affirmative only-use wording and complementary other-purpose prohibitions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use limitation and the text identifying the permitted purpose; include a governing introduction when the rule is listed.
